protocols.name: Swallowed poison or chemicals
exemplars: my toddler drank some bleach
kid swallowed grandma's pills
he drank antifreeze by accident
child ate laundry detergent pod
she swallowed a button battery
someone swallowed rat poison what do i do
he got paint thinner in his mouth
she took a whole bottle of sleeping pills

identify_poison.text: Take the container, packet or plant with you and keep it — knowing WHAT and HOW MUCH decides the treatment. Note the time it happened.

clear_mouth.text: If anything is still in their mouth, have them spit it out. Wipe the mouth gently with a cloth.
donot: Do NOT make them vomit — it burns twice on the way back up and can choke them.
Do not give salt water, milk, or charcoal unless poison control tells you to.
Do not give anything to drink unless poison control says so.

q_conscious_poison.prompt: Are they awake and breathing normally?

recovery_poison.text: Roll them into the recovery position on their side so they cannot choke, and watch their breathing constantly.

poison_center.text: While waiting for help, call your poison center if you have the number — in the US, 1-800-222-1222 — and follow their instructions exactly. A button battery swallowed is always an immediate emergency, even with no symptoms.

monitor_poison.text: Keep the container ready to hand over. Tell me immediately if they vomit, become drowsy, have a seizure, or their breathing changes.

q_battery.prompt: Did they swallow a button battery — a small flat disc battery, like from a watch, remote, or toy?

battery_honey.text: A swallowed button battery burns through the food pipe within hours — get to an emergency department NOW, even with no symptoms. On the way: if the child is over 1 year old, swallowed it within the last 12 hours, and can swallow, give 2 teaspoons of ordinary honey every 10 minutes, up to 6 doses.
donot: Do not delay leaving for the hospital to find honey.
Do not give honey to a baby under 1 year.
Do not give any other food or drink.

monitor_battery.text: Head for emergency care now and bring the battery packaging if you have it. Tell me immediately if they vomit, cough blood, or become drowsy.

protocols.name: Carbon monoxide / toxic fumes
exemplars: our carbon monoxide alarm is going off and we feel dizzy
everyone in the house has a headache and feels sick
he was running the generator in the garage and passed out
gas leak my roommate is nauseous
she breathed a lot of smoke in the fire

get_out_co.text: Get everyone — including yourself — into fresh air NOW. Open doors on your way out if quick and safe. Do not stay to find the source.
donot: Do not go back inside for belongings or pets.
Do not light anything or flip switches if you smell gas.

count_heads.text: Outside, count that everyone is out. If someone is still inside, tell the emergency operator — do NOT go back in yourself; rescuers have air tanks.

q_conscious_co.prompt: Is everyone awake and breathing normally?

q_breathing_co.prompt: For the person who is not awake — are they breathing normally?

to_cpr_co.text: We start CPR now, in the fresh air.

recovery_co.text: Recovery position on their side, in fresh air, and watch their breathing constantly.

rest_co.text: Keep everyone resting quietly in fresh air — exertion worsens the poisoning. Everyone exposed should be checked by the medics, even if feeling better: CO effects can linger and rebound.

monitor_co.text: Nobody goes back inside until professionals declare it safe. Tell me if anyone develops headache, confusion, chest pain or drowsiness.

protocols.name: Alcohol poisoning
exemplars: my friend drank way too much and won't wake up
he passed out drunk and is breathing weird
alcohol poisoning at a party what do i do
she is blackout drunk and vomiting while lying down
college kid unresponsive after shots

q_responsive_alc.prompt: Do they respond when you shout their name and shake their shoulder — even just groaning?

q_breathing_alc.prompt: Watch their chest for up to 10 seconds — breathing normally, at least 8 breaths a minute, no long gaps?

recovery_alc.text: Roll them into the recovery position on their side so vomit cannot choke them. Cover them with a blanket — alcohol drains body heat.
donot: Do not leave them alone or let them sleep it off on their back.
Do not give coffee, food, or a cold shower — none of it sobers anyone and it can harm them.
Do not try to make them vomit.

recovery_alc_awake.text: Keep them on their side, warm, and watched. Give small sips of water only if they are properly awake and can swallow.
donot: Do not leave them alone.
Do not give coffee or a cold shower.
Do not let them drink more alcohol.

monitor_alc.text: Check their breathing every few minutes until help arrives. Tell me immediately if breathing slows, they gasp, they cannot be woken at all, or they have a seizure.

protocols.name: Snake bite
exemplars: a snake just bit my leg
rattlesnake bite on his ankle
my dog scared up a snake and it bit my son
bitten by a snake while hiking what do i do
snake bite is swelling fast

away_snake.text: Move away from the snake — do not try to catch or kill it. A photo from a safe distance helps identification, but only if easy.

still_calm_sb.text: Keep them STILL and calm — movement pumps venom through the body. Sit or lie them down and keep the bitten limb still, below heart level, supported like a broken bone.
donot: Do not cut the wound or try to suck out venom.
Do not apply ice or a tourniquet.
Do not give alcohol, caffeine, or painkillers like ibuprofen or aspirin.

remove_tight_sb.text: Remove rings, watches and tight clothing near the bite now — before swelling. Mark the edge of the swelling on the skin with a pen and the time, if you can.

clean_cover_sb.text: Cover the bite with a clean, loose dressing. Keep the person warm and completely at rest. If they must be moved to reach help, carry them — walking spreads venom.

monitor_sb.text: Keep them still until help arrives. Tell me immediately if they have trouble breathing, drooping eyelids, vomiting, severe swelling, or become drowsy — and if you are in Australia, tell the operator: a firm pressure bandage over the whole limb is used there for some snakes.

protocols.name: Bee / wasp / insect sting
exemplars: i got stung by a bee on my hand
wasp stung my kid on the neck
bee sting the stinger is still in
stung by a hornet it is swelling
multiple wasp stings while gardening

q_allergy_sting.prompt: Critical check: do they have a known severe allergy, or any trouble breathing, tongue or throat swelling, widespread hives, dizziness or vomiting?

to_ana_sting.text: That is a severe reaction — we treat it as anaphylaxis now.

remove_stinger.text: If the stinger is still in the skin, scrape it out sideways NOW with a fingernail or a card edge — speed matters more than method.
donot: Do not squeeze the venom sac with tweezers or fingers.

cold_sting.text: Wash with soap and water, then hold a wrapped cold pack on it for 10 to 20 minutes. Remove rings if the hand was stung.

soothe_sting.text: For itch and swelling: an oral antihistamine at packet dose, or hydrocortisone cream on the spot. Swelling can grow for a day or two — that alone is not an allergy.

monitor_sting.text: Watch them for the next hour. Tell me immediately if breathing trouble, throat or tongue swelling, spreading hives, or faintness appear. Stings in the mouth or throat, or more than a few stings at once, need urgent medical care — suck ice and seek help for mouth stings.

protocols.name: Spider bite
exemplars: a spider bit me and it really hurts
black widow bite what do i do
bitten by a brown spider in the shed
spider bite is getting red and painful
funnel web spider bit him

q_dangerous_spider.prompt: Could it be a highly venomous spider — black widow, redback, brown recluse, or an Australian funnel-web — or are there severe symptoms: intense pain, cramping, sweating, vomiting, trouble breathing?

ems_spider.text: Call emergency services or poison control now. Keep them still and calm. For a suspected Australian funnel-web, apply a firm pressure bandage over the bite and up the limb, and keep it completely still; for other spiders, no pressure bandage — just a cold pack.

monitor_spider_sev.text: Keep them at rest. Tell me if pain spreads, muscles cramp, or breathing changes.

wash_spider.text: Wash the bite with soap and water. Apply a wrapped cold pack for 10 to 15 minutes to ease pain and swelling.
donot: Do not cut the bite or try to suck anything out.
Do not apply heat.

monitor_spider.text: Most spider bites settle like a bad sting. See a doctor if pain grows over hours, cramps or sweating start, a blister or dark center forms, or redness keeps spreading over days. Bring the spider or a photo if it is safely possible.

protocols.name: Tick bite / removal
exemplars: there is a tick attached to my leg
how do i remove a tick from my kid
found a tick on the dog and on me
tick bite after hiking what should i do
tick buried in the skin

remove_tick.text: Use fine-tipped tweezers. Grip the tick as close to the skin as possible — by the head, not the body — and pull straight upward with slow, steady pressure. No twisting or jerking.
donot: Do not burn the tick with a match.
Do not smother it with vaseline, nail polish or alcohol while attached.
Do not squeeze its body.

after_tick.text: Clean the bite and your hands with soap and water or alcohol. If mouth parts remain in the skin and will not lift out easily with tweezers, leave them — the skin will expel them.

save_tick.text: Note today's date. If you want, keep the tick in a sealed bag in case a doctor wants to identify it. Flush or bag it — do not crush it with fingers.

monitor_tick.text: Watch the area for the next month. See a doctor promptly for: a spreading or bulls-eye rash, fever, aches, unusual tiredness, or if the tick was attached over 24 hours — early antibiotics prevent Lyme disease. In Australia, allergic reactions to ticks matter: for known tick allergy, freeze-spray kits and medical removal are preferred.

protocols.name: Animal or human bite
exemplars: a dog bit my hand it broke the skin
stray cat bit my daughter
bitten by a bat while camping
neighbor's dog attacked and bit his leg
someone bit me in a fight and it broke skin

q_severe_bite.prompt: Is it bleeding heavily, gaping open, on the face, neck, hands or genitals, or was the animal wild, stray, or acting strangely?

severe_bite_path.text: Control heavy bleeding first: press hard with a clean cloth. This bite needs professional care today — call emergency services for heavy bleeding, otherwise go straight to urgent care.

wash_bite.text: Wash the wound thoroughly under running water with soap for a full 15 minutes — this is the single best protection against rabies and infection. Pat dry and cover with a clean dressing.
donot: Do not close the wound with tape or glue.
Do not ignore a cat bite or deep puncture — they infect deeply.

rabies_check.text: Rabies check: if the animal was wild, stray, unvaccinated, or a bat — even a tiny bat scratch — medical care TODAY for possible rabies shots is essential. Rabies is fatal once symptoms start, and the shots work only before that.

tetanus_bite.text: Any bite that breaks skin deserves a medical review within 24 hours — many need antibiotics, and a tetanus booster if theirs is over 5 years old.

monitor_bite.text: Watch for infection over the next days: spreading redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or fever means see a doctor immediately. If the animal can be safely observed or reported, tell animal control.

protocols.name: Jellyfish sting
exemplars: i got stung by a jellyfish at the beach
jellyfish tentacles wrapped around her leg
box jellyfish sting emergency
man of war stung him badly
stung by something in the sea it burns

out_of_water_jf.text: Get them out of the water and keep them still. Rinse the area with SEAWATER — not fresh water, which fires more stingers.
donot: Do not rinse with fresh water.
Do not rub the area with sand or a towel.
Do not urinate on it — that is a myth and can make it worse.

q_dangerous_jf.prompt: Are you in tropical waters — northern Australia, Indo-Pacific — or is the person having chest pain, trouble breathing, or collapsing?

ems_jf.text: Call emergency services now. In tropical Australia, flood the sting with VINEGAR for at least 30 seconds if available. Be ready to start CPR if they collapse.

remove_tentacles_sev.text: Remove any tentacles with tweezers or a gloved hand — not bare fingers. Keep them still and monitor closely.

monitor_jf_sev.text: Watch them constantly. Tell me immediately if breathing changes or they stop responding — we start CPR straight away.

remove_tentacles.text: Pluck off any visible tentacles with tweezers or a stick — not bare hands. Rinse again with seawater.

hot_water_jf.text: Immerse the sting in hot water — as hot as comfortable, about 42 to 45 degrees Celsius — for 20 to 45 minutes. No hot water? A cold pack helps the pain instead.

monitor_jf.text: Pain should ease over the next hour. See a doctor if it covers a large area, involves the face or genitals, blisters badly, or any dizziness, nausea or breathing trouble appears — tell me right away if those start.
